method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the writing-l4-rules skill; the duties with deadlines in ss 18, 269 and 23/27 are regulative rules (PARTY ... MUST/DO ... WITHIN ... LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE) run inside plain-fact questions; no REFUSE (gaps answer `not covered` or NOTHING, asserted); every satisfaction or opinion of the Tribunal, the decision-maker or the Attorney-General asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. First encoding of this Act. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024, No. 40, 2024, Compilation No. 5, compilation date 2026-05-18 (register id C2026C00202; Federal Register of Legislation, retrieved 2026-10-13), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2024A00040.txt. No instrument brought in: the Administrative Review Tribunal Rules and the practice directions are not deposited, so their numbers are inputs.

checks.result: 197 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings; 3 #TRACEs each a BREACH as its expect line says (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A breached DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so traces are asserted through a CONSIDER ... WHEN FULFILLED helper and breaches are #TRACEd.

scope: From the applicant's seat (a person affected by a reviewable Commonwealth decision, such as a refused or reduced compensation or benefit claim): ss 12, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 23, 27, 28(3)-(9), 29, 31, 32, 66, 84, 95-102, 107, 108(3)-(5), 111, 112(5)-(7), 123, 125, 131C, 131D, 131G, 131H, 131J, 131W, 131X, 172-174, 266, 268-271, 294; ss 65(2), 83(2), (4) named. Out: Parts 1-2; ss 13, 14, 21, 22, 24-26, 28(10), 30, 33-35; Part 4 Divs 3-4 and ss 49-65 (except 65(2)), 67-94 (procedure, hearings, evidence, certificates); ss 103, 105, 106, 109, 110, 113-120; ss 121, 122, 126-131; Part 5A ss 131E, 131F, 131K-131V; Part 6; ss 175-191; Parts 8-9; ss 267, 272; Part 11 except s 294 (incl. s 292 short periods and s 296 fees).
seat: the applicant (a person whose interests are affected by a reviewable Commonwealth decision, who seeks reasons, applies to the Administrative Review Tribunal and may go on to the guidance and appeals panel, second review or the Federal Court; in s 84, the person stepping in for an applicant who has died or become bankrupt)
